title: Vaihdettu osa ja korjattu auto
subtitle: A changed part and a fixed car

blocks.text: Lesson 3 gave you the active participle: ei toiminut, 'didn't work' — describing what a subject itself did or didn't do. There's a second participle, the passive one, that instead describes something that was done TO a noun — and it slots in front of that noun just like an ordinary adjective.

blocks.translation: A changed part and a fixed car.

blocks.title: The passive participle as everyday adjective
blocks.text: English does this too — 'a fixed car', 'a changed part' — participles routinely double as adjectives. Finnish leans on this constantly in reviews, since it's a compact way to describe a part or car's history in a single word, right before naming it.

blocks.content: Where the active participle from Lesson 3 ends in -nut/-nyt (toiminut, 'having worked' — done by the subject), the passive participle ends in {-ttu|grammar|passive participle suffix|done to (past)} or -tty — describing something done to the noun. Vaihtaa (to change) → {vaihdettu|grammar|passive participle|changed}. Korjata (to fix) → {korjattu|grammar|passive participle|fixed}.

items.en: The fixed car broke down on the way home.

blocks.text: Piece 2 — This ending should look familiar

blocks.title: You've already met this shape
blocks.text: Compare -ttu/-tty to Lesson 4's passive past -ttiin/-tiin: vaihdettiin (was changed, an event) versus vaihdettu (changed, a description). Same underlying passive family — one form reports an action happening, the other freezes that action into a descriptive word you can plant in front of a noun.

items.fi: Eilen {vaihdettu|grammar|passive participle, description|changed} osa on jo rikki.
items.en: The part changed yesterday is already broken.

blocks.content: Since the passive participle behaves like an ordinary adjective, it follows Lesson 28's agreement rule too — it takes whatever case its noun takes. En luota {vaihdettuun|grammar|illative, agreeing participle|changed} osaan — 'I don't trust the changed part' — both words bending into the illative together.

items.en: I don't trust the changed part.
I talked about the fixed car.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Did the changed part work well?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Ei. Korjattu auto hajosi jo kotimatkalla.
lines.en: No. The fixed car broke down already on the way home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Do you still trust the changed part?

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: I don't trust it at all.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: Active participle (-nut/-nyt, Lesson 3) answers 'what did the subject do or not do?'. Passive participle (-ttu/-tty, this lesson) answers 'what was done to this noun?'. Ask yourself which question a participle is answering, and you'll always know which one you're looking at.

blocks.content: Vaihdettu: VAIH-det-tu (three syllables, the 'vaih' rhymes with English 'my'). Korjattu: KOR-yat-tu (double t held). Vaihdettuun: VAIH-det-tuun (long final 'uun' — the illative ending stretching the word).

rows.en: passive participle suffix — 'done to' as an adjective
